reportMarkdown:
# Post Lazy Semantics CPU Profile

One headed Chromium/WebGPU CPU-profile process passed at DPR 1 and DPR 2 with exact DataTable final offsets, established renderer/layout/text/style invariants, and zero terminal errors.

`DevtoolsSemantics` drop sampled at 12.474 ms (DPR 1) and 9.329 ms (DPR 2), versus 11.164/15.867 ms in experiment 82. This is +11.73%/-41.21%, a mixed sampled result. Lazy optional storage removes all default payloads by construction, but authored semantics still own strings/vectors and therefore retain a visible teardown family. The profile does not justify further semantics lifecycle complexity.

The strongest repeatable next cleanup family is Taffy measured-closure teardown plus dirty propagation:

| Metric | DPR 1 | DPR 2 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `TaffyLayoutEngine::clear` | 118.001 ms | 129.056 ms |
| measured `StackSafe<Box<FnMut>>` drop | 64.647 ms | 71.033 ms |
| `mark_dirty_recursive` | 34.659 ms | 37.679 ms |

`Scene::clear` measured 12.477/26.828 ms, DispatchTree clear 15.629/14.225 ms, and element-state table clear 13.939/22.017 ms. Taffy's overlapping per-measured-node dirty propagation is the highest-confidence next research target; any change must preserve closure release and layout invalidation.

No product or test source changed.
decisionMarkdown:
# Decision

Accept the profile as read-only evidence. Keep lazy optional frame semantics, but do not add another semantics lifecycle mechanism: sampled authored-payload teardown remains and the two-DPR movement is mixed. Next inspect whether `TaffyLayoutEngine::clear` redundantly propagates dirty state once per measured leaf and whether one bounded root/node invalidation can preserve exact semantics.
